thread:
runtime_oncall: :rotating_light: seeing a spike of container crashes on gpu-pool-3, lots of CUDA illegal memory access logs. paging / OOM noise too. root pod names: model-svc-74ff, model-svc-74gg. tagging SRE
SRE_Lead: on it. can you paste the last few dmesg lines and kubectl describe?
runtime_oncall: dmesg snippet:
```
[13045.123456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID=23112, 0a(0), Ch 00000010, Voluntary command submission
[13045.123458] cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7ffdeadbeef
[13045.123459] golden_driver: pagewalk: unaligned deviceaddr 0x7f89abcde000
[13045.123460] oom-killer: kill process 23112 (model-server) score 987
```
runtime_oncall: kubectl describe pod model-svc-74ff:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----     ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning  BackOff    2m    kubelet, node-10    Back-off restarting failed container
  Warning  Evicted    1m    kubelet, node-10    Pod evicted due to node pressure
```
eng_runtime: thanks. seeing pattern similar to the pagewalk misalignment we saw last month but mutated. multiple pods on same node failing, not just one container. may be a kernel/SMMU walk race. tagging @eng-ml for model impact.
eng_ml: model inference latency spiking; fallback model variant (cpu-quant) is available but lower Q. we can route small % as canary.
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-4872 (cuda_illegal_mem_access). Severity: High. PagerDuty triggered.
PagerDutyBot: PagerDuty alert: runtime_oncall is on-call for incidents. Acknowledge?
runtime_oncall: acknowledged. starting triage: 1) cordon node-10 2) evict pods 3) failover traffic to node pool-4 4) collect full kernel oops and nvcrash logs.
infra_eng: cordoning node-10 now -> `kubectl cordon node-10` ; draining with `kubectl drain node-10 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
SRE_Lead: good. we should also reduce batch sizes and disable large prefilling to avoid OOMs while we triage. eng_runtime can you push emergency config?
eng_runtime: rolling config change to reduce max_batch_tokens=128 and max_concurrency_per_gpu=2. patching canary first on pool-4.
runtime_oncall: attaching nvcrash log + container logs:
```
E 2026-03-12T09:14:21.345Z model-server[23112]: runtime error: Illegal memory access in attention_kernel.cu:234
E 2026-03-12T09:14:21.346Z model-server[23112]: stack trace:
  at attention_kernel (attention_kernel.cu:234)
  at decode_step (decoding.cpp:512)
  at worker_loop (server.cpp:88)
```
runtime_oncall: also seeing repeated: `pagewalk: unaligned deviceaddr` in kernel logs. looks like mapping instability during heavy pagewalks.
eng_runtime: can you confirm GPU driver version and whether any recent kernel modules landed?
infra_eng: driver: 535.86, kernel: 6.2.15, no kernel grub updates in last 24h. we did roll out a container runtime update 3 hours ago (runc 1.1.1 -> 1.2.0).
SRE_Lead: hmmm. runc update could change mmap/pinning behavior but illegal memory access from GPU usually points at kernel or driver SMMU interactions. create hypothesis list: 1) kernel SMMU pagewalk race under pressure 2) driver/firmware combo regression 3) model change triggering out-of-bounds read due to OOM-induced stale pointers
eng_ml: ops - we rolled a model graph tweak ~2h ago (reordered KV caching). could that change memory access patterns?
eng_runtime: possible. but the kernel message about unaligned deviceaddr suggests the device virtual address translation returned an unexpected alignment. that smells like page-table corruption or concurrent update.
runtime_oncall: mitigation so far: cordoned node-10, drained, restarted model pods on pool-4. rolling back model graph tweak on canary 1.
eng_runtime: initiating hotfix: set environment var REDWOOD_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1 on runtime pods to reduce prefetch-induced pagewalks. patch applied to canary. monitoring.
runtime_oncall: canary looks stable for 4 minutes, no crashes so far. traffic shifted 20% to fallback.
SRE_Lead: good. next: collect full vmcore from node-10 before repro. liaise with infra to capture crash kernels.
infra_eng: capturing vmcore now with makedumpfile. ETA ~8m. also saving /var/log/nvidia and dmesg.
eng_runtime: we should also disable aggressive batch fusion in the runtime (quick flag: --disable-fusion) while we observe. dropping fusion on canary.
eng_ml: customer impact: two customers saw 502s for ~3-7 minutes, one had spike in error rate (customer-id: acme-corp). drafting customer message.
customer_success: draft: "We're investigating an infrastructure issue causing intermittent inference errors. We've shifted your traffic to a fallback pool and are monitoring. We'll follow up with an incident summary within 2 hours." ok?
SRE_Lead: fine. mark P0 status, assign postmortem owner to eng_runtime.
eng_runtime: taking postmortem. adding todo: reproduce with stress tester, instrument SMMU translations, and add more guard checks in attention kernel code.
runtime_oncall: timeline so far:
- 09:12:30 alarm: OOM + illegal memory access on node-10
- 09:13:05 pods restarted and evicted
- 09:17:40 cordon/drain started
- 09:20:10 config patch reduce batching applied canary
- 09:24:00 REDWOOD_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1 applied to canary
- 09:29:12 canary stable, traffic shifted
- 09:32:40 vmcore dump start

eng_runtime: logs from canary after prefetch disable show no cuda Xid 31 or illegal mem for ~12m.
infra_eng: vmcore captured and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-2026-4872/node-10-vmcore. kernel oops included.
runtime_oncall: attaching pointer to nvcrash bundle and model-server logs in thread.
eng_ml: reenable small percentage of traffic to original variant to check quality regression; will watch error rates.
SRE_Lead: moving into recovery phase. next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned until we have kernel oops analysis 2) run stress repro on a staging node with the same driver/kernel + runc versions 3) if repro, coordinate kernel module rollback or driver upgrade with infra
eng_runtime: for immediate safety let's push a node taint to prevent scheduling heavy GPU-prefetch workloads: `kubectl taint nodes node-11 gpu-prefetch=disabled:NoSchedule`
runtime_oncall: applied taint on node-11 and node-12 as precaution.
customer_success: sent initial message to acme-corp and 2 other affected customers.
eng_ml: small update: when we ramped back 10% to original model, got two more 502s then stabilized. suspicious timing matches model graph change + heavy prefetch.
SRE_Lead: hypothesis leaning towards a combination: prefetch+fusion causing pathological pagewalk bursts exposing kernel SMMU bug (race) leading to unaligned deviceaddr and subsequent CUDA illegal memory access.
eng_runtime: agree. mitigation plan: keep prefetch disabled, disable fusion, keep reduced batch sizes, keep affected nodes cordoned. longer term: add pagewalk alignment checks in kernel help? need upstream kernel/driver discussion.
runtime_oncall: assigning follow ups:
- eng_runtime: postmortem + reproducibility (owner)
- infra_eng: prepare kernel/driver repro env and coordinate with cloud vendor (owner)
- eng_ml: rollback model graph tweak and add memory-safety tests (owner)
- customer_success: update customers with ETA for full report in 2h (owner)
SRE_Lead: if any sign of recurrence, escalate to SEV1 and consider rolling kernel downgrade to previous known-good.
runtime_oncall: will keep monitoring. currently error rates back to baseline for most customers. closing initial triage, leaving channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
